title: Biblical Circle, Boundary, Return & Escape — Addendum
purpose: Extend the repository's biblical overlap layer with texts showing that circles, cycles, boundaries and return can signify very different structures: creation-order, destructive recurrence, encirclement, trapping, threshold, escape and ascent.
interpretive_rule: Do not flatten every circle into imprisonment or every Dog into hostility. The texts below supply distinct functions; Potatoverse geometry is a later comparative synthesis.

proverbs_26_11.structure: dog returns to vomit ↔ fool repeats folly

2_peter_2_22.structure: dog returns to vomit; washed sow returns to mire

james_3_6.structure: the tongue is described as setting ablaze the course/cycle of life; English translations vary
james_3_6.project_use: secondary comparator for a destructive process that propagates through a life-system
james_3_6.caution: Preserve translation variation; do not build doctrine on one English rendering alone.

proverbs_8_27.structure: Wisdom is present when God marks/inscribes a circle on the face of the deep in several translations
proverbs_8_27.project_use: Circle can signify imposed order/boundary rather than prison.

job_26_10.structure: a boundary/circle is marked on the waters at the limit of light and darkness in several translations
job_26_10.project_use: Circumference as ordered limit and differentiation.

psalm_22_16_20.structure: dogs/hostile company surround the suffering speaker
psalm_22_16_20.project_use: perimeter pressure around a suffering center

psalm_40_2.project_use: closed lower condition is escapable; stable standing follows extraction

psalm_69_2_14.project_use: mud as trapping medium without making mud metaphysically evil

proverbs_5_22.project_use: repeated action can generate its own binding

proverbs_29_6.project_use: trap can emerge from the pattern itself

psalm_9_15.structure: nations fall into the pit they made

psalm_141_9_10.structure: traps are laid; speaker seeks passage while trap-setters fall into their own nets
psalm_141_9_10.project_use: exit and inversion of the trap

john_10_9.structure: entry through Jesus-as-door leads to salvation/pasture

matthew_7_13_14.project_use: not every trajectory is equivalent; passage has direction and consequence

luke_13_24.structure: strive to enter through narrow door
luke_13_24.project_use: being near a threshold is not the same as crossing it

genesis_28_12_17.structure: ladder between earth/heaven + house of God + gate of heaven

ezekiel_1_15_21.structure: wheel-within-wheel / intersecting wheel imagery coordinated with living creatures and spirit
ezekiel_1_15_21.project_use: cyclic motion can be integrated with axis/order rather than closed recurrence

ezekiel_10.structure: cherubim, wheels and divine chariot imagery

mark_7_24_30_matthew_15_21_28.structure: household-dog/bread metaphor occurs in a dialogue where outsider status is not terminal
mark_7_24_30_matthew_15_21_28.project_use: Dog-boundary can be transformed; category is relational, not permanent essence

luke_16_20_21.structure: dogs lick Lazarus's sores while he lies at the rich man's gate
luke_16_20_21.project_use: complicates Dog symbolism: Dog can appear at the bodily/social boundary of an excluded sufferer rather than only as attacker
luke_16_20_21.caution: The text does not straightforwardly assign the dogs a moral role; retain ambiguity.

revelation_22_15.structure: dogs appear outside the restored city

revelation_21_22.structure: measured city + gates + river + tree + life
revelation_21_22.project_use: destination state where boundary and access coexist with life and order

derived_project_distinctions.distinction: circle names a closed geometry; orbit adds movement around a center
orbit can avoid the center/intersection; vesica exists because two domains intersect
wheel is recurrence coordinated by an axle/axis; loop need not have orienting structure
spiral repeats while changing level/radius/position; circle returns to equivalent position
wall separates; door preserves boundary while permitting passage
both are below; mud can trap while root transforms the below into nourishment and growth
